item.title: NEW: Polymarket Loses $2.7M in Supply Chain Attack via DebugBear
item.description:
Headline: Polymarket Loses $2.7M in Supply Chain Attack via DebugBear

Summary:
The prediction market platform Polymarket suspended trading on October 29, 2026, after a supply chain attack involving a compromised third-party script from DebugBear resulted in approximately $2.71 million in unauthorized withdrawals. Attackers injected malicious JavaScript into DebugBear's Real User Monitoring (RUM) script, allowing them to hijack active user sessions on Polymarket's international site. The malicious code executed trades and transferred funds without stealing user credentials. Polymarket has pledged to reimburse all affected users.

Severity: High

Categories: Supply Chain Attack, Cyberattack, Data Breach

Article Type: NewsArticle

Reading Time: 5 minutes

Meta Description: Prediction market Polymarket lost $2.71 million in a supply chain attack on October 29, 2026. A compromised script from vendor DebugBear was used to steal funds.

item.title: NEW: Trojanized 'Claude Code' VS Code Extension Installs SSH Backdoor
item.description:
Headline: Trojanized 'Claude Code' VS Code Extension Installs SSH Backdoor

Summary:
A malicious version of the 'Claude Code' VS Code extension, distributed via the Cursor IDE marketplace, installed a persistent SSH backdoor on developers' machines. The trojanized update, version 2.1.313, affected up to 5,000 users by adding an attacker-controlled public SSH key to the 'authorized_keys' file. The malicious package was active for several hours on October 29, 2026, before being removed. Users are urged to check their systems for the unauthorized key and rotate all credentials.

Severity: High

Categories: Supply Chain Attack, Malware, Threat Intelligence

item.title: NEW: Palo Alto Firewalls Under Attack via PHP2Shell RCE Flaws
item.description:
Headline: Palo Alto Firewalls Under Attack via PHP2Shell RCE Flaws

Summary:
Palo Alto Networks confirmed its PAN-OS firewalls are being actively exploited by attackers chaining two critical PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively known as PHP2Shell. The attackers are combining these with a Linux kernel flaw (CVE-2026-46300) to gain root access on devices with exposed management interfaces. The attack allows for full device takeover, credential theft, and internal network pivoting. Palo Alto Networks is contacting affected customers.

Severity: Critical

item.title: NEW: Chinese APT Exploited VMware ESXi Zero-Day to Evade Logs
item.description:
Headline: Chinese APT Exploited VMware ESXi Zero-Day to Evade Logs

Summary:
The China-nexus espionage group Warp Panda exploited a VMware ESXi zero-day (CVE-2026-41709) to hide their activities within victim networks. The vulnerability, an insufficient logging flaw, allowed the APT group to perform actions on virtual machines without leaving a proper audit trail. The flaw was used in attacks against U.S. organizations, including in the legal sector. CISA has since added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating a patch for federal agencies.

item.title: NEW: Akamai: AI-Driven Scams Double, Phishing Attack Lifespan Halved
item.description:
Headline: Akamai: AI-Driven Scams Double, Phishing Attack Lifespan Halved

Summary:
A new report from Akamai reveals that AI-powered online scams doubled in volume in Q1 2026, surpassing traditional phishing attacks for the first time. The study, 'AI-Driven Digital Deception,' also found that the operational lifespan of phishing campaigns has shrunk by over 50% to just 22 days due to automation and Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) toolkits. High-technology and financial services companies remain the most impersonated sectors, highlighting a rapidly evolving threat landscape where speed and scale are increasing dramatically.

item.title: NEW: FDD Urges NIST, NSA to Evaluate New Anti-Ransomware Tech
item.description:
Headline: FDD Urges NIST, NSA to Evaluate New Anti-Ransomware Tech

Summary:
On October 30, 2026, the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD) urged NIST and the NSA to evaluate 'vaultless, keyless pseudonymization' as a safeguard against ransomware and data breaches. The think tank argues that this technology, which replaces sensitive data with non-sensitive tokens, could render stolen data valueless to attackers, addressing the vulnerability of data when it is decrypted for use. The FDD is advocating for a shift in cybersecurity policy to focus on making data less damaging when breaches inevitably occur.

Severity: Informational

Categories: Policy and Compliance, Regulatory, Ransomware

item.description:
Headline: U.S. Bill Aims to Bolster Cloud Security Standards via NIST

Summary:
U.S. Representative Rich McCormick introduced the 'Common-Sense Cloud Security Act' on October 29, 2026. The bill directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop updated cybersecurity standards for cloud services, with a focus on protecting critical infrastructure and sensitive data. The legislation calls for collaboration between government and industry to address modern cloud vulnerabilities, including insecure east-west traffic and risks from third-party applications, and to promote the use of AI for threat detection.

item.title: NEW: Critical PHP 'PHP2Shell' Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild
item.description:
Headline: Critical PHP 'PHP2Shell' Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild

Summary:
Two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are being actively exploited. Dubbed 'PHP2Shell,' these flaws carry a CVSS score of 9.2 and affect the widely used scripting language, impacting countless web servers and content management systems. Threat actors are reportedly targeting internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces by chaining the PHP vulnerabilities with a Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw to gain root access. Palo Alto Networks has identified over 22.6 million potentially vulnerable instances and urges immediate patching and mitigation.

Severity: Critical

item.title: UPDATE: Critical PHP RCE Vulnerabilities (PHP2Shell) Expose Millions of Servers
item.description:
Headline: Critical PHP RCE Vulnerabilities (PHP2Shell) Expose Millions of Servers

Summary:
Two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, have been disclosed in PHP, a ubiquitous server-side scripting language. Dubbed 'PHP2Shell,' both vulnerabilities carry a critical CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2. Security researchers at Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 have identified over 22.6 million internet-exposed instances that are potentially vulnerable. While an initial report linking these vulnerabilities to an attack on a European government agency has been retracted due to a lack of confirmation, the widespread use of PHP in web servers and content management systems makes these flaws a significant global threat. Organizations are strongly urged to assess their exposure and apply patches immediately to mitigate the risk of full server compromise.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management, Threat Intelligence

item.title: UPDATE: iRhythm Notifies Over 360,000 Patients of Data Breach from June
item.description:
Headline: iRhythm Notifies Over 360,000 Patients of Data Breach from June

Summary:
Medical device maker iRhythm Technologies is notifying over 360,000 patients that their personal and medical data was stolen in a data breach that occurred in June 2026. The incident involved unauthorized access to business applications hosted by a third party. Attackers accessed and exfiltrated data between June 3 and June 8, then contacted iRhythm on June 9 with a ransom demand. The compromised data includes patient names, addresses, dates of birth, insurance information, and device serial numbers. Notifications to affected individuals began on October 2, 2026, nearly four months after the breach.

Severity: High

Categories: Data Breach, Supply Chain Attack, Regulatory

Article Type: NewsArticle
